detaileddescription.para: It is common to express the dynamics of network agents as a single function according to which each agent's state vector evolves, and have their state vectors and void* params refer to parameters. In the Kuramoto model, for example, each vertex has a unit state vector containing its phase $\theta$, with its void* params containing its eigenfrequency, and evolves according to the agentic Kuramoto model. In the swing equation, each vertex has a two-component state vector containing its phase $\theta$ and frequency $\omega$, and evolves according to the swing equation. There is, however, no strict requirement saying agents must:

listitem.para: Depend on the same time-variant parameters as others
Evolve according to the same dynamics, noise, or discrete callback functions

detaileddescription.para: Whenever one or more of the first three conditions is false, the agents are said to be heterogeneous (initial conditions and constants are usually unique by default). This gives rise to the term "heterogeneous dynamics", simply meaning that two or more agents in the network do not exhibit common dynamics. This can be, for example:

listitem.para: One node evolving according to the Kuramoto model, its neighbour to the swing equation
One node being static, its neighbour dynamic
One node being stochastic, its neighbour purely deterministic
One node having a ten-element state vector, its neighbour a scalar state

detaileddescription.para: NDXL makes simulating heterogeneous dynamics easy by assigning agent properties directly to the agents themselves, as outlined in the Heterogeneous Dynamics example.
